title: VIP feature signal synthesis and release negotiation lab
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Objective: Create a reproducible "hypothesis-to-commit" playbook for top-account feature asks that combines signal synthesis, measurable success criteria, and a guarded negotiation protocol. The goal is to avoid ad-hoc promises to VIP customers by translating requests into testable product hypotheses, required investments (engineering/design/ops), and contractual runway options (pilot, timeboxed commit, or buy-down feature). This ticket runs a small internal 'negotiation lab' with 3 active accounts to validate the process and tooling.
success_metrics: Percent of VIP asks converted to hypothesis + metric (target 95%)
Time between initial ask and firm commitment (target median <= 21 days)
Rate of scope rollback or re-negotiation post-commit (target <= 10%)
Delta in estimated vs actual engineering effort for lab cases (target within +/-20%)
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step negotiation script and templates
Three pilot VIP accounts run through lab with signed timeboxed commitments or formal deferrals
Designs and acceptance tests attached for each pilot feature
Engineering capacity and cost estimate recorded and validated by ENG lead
Template contractual language reviewed by Legal and Customer Success
